qualify_source.call: verify.qualify_source {doi: "10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2023.56070", question: "Do digital health interventions lower blood pressure in US populations experiencing health disparities?"}

check_claim_same_direction.claim: In populations experiencing health disparities, digital health interventions for hypertension were associated with a 4.24 mm Hg greater reduction in systolic blood pressure at 6 months than control.
check_claim_same_direction.passage: Between the intervention and control groups, there were statistically significant mean differences in SBP at 6 months (-4.24 mm Hg; 95% CI, -7.33 to -1.14 mm Hg; P = .01) and SBP changes at 12 months (-4.30 mm Hg; 95% CI, -8.38 to -0.23 mm Hg; P = .04).

check_claim_negated.claim: In populations experiencing health disparities, digital health interventions for hypertension showed no difference in systolic blood pressure at 6 months compared with control.
check_claim_negated.passage: Between the intervention and control groups, there were statistically significant mean differences in SBP at 6 months (-4.24 mm Hg; 95% CI, -7.33 to -1.14 mm Hg; P = .01) and SBP changes at 12 months (-4.30 mm Hg; 95% CI, -8.38 to -0.23 mm Hg; P = .04).
